### workspace finish --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace finish [--name WS] [--pr] [--json] [project]

Verify a worktree project is clean and fully pushed, then remove it
the same way 'workspace kill' does (session, worktree, config, state).

If no project is given (positionally or with --name), finishes the workspace
the current directory is in: a worktree's .workspace-project marker, else the
active workspace whose root holds it. Outside any workspace it refuses
(not_in_workspace).

Refuses when the branch has uncommitted changes to tracked files
(untracked files don't count), has no upstream, or is ahead of its
upstream. There is no override; push or commit first.

Options:
        --name NAME                  The worktree workspace to finish (default: the one detected from the current directory)
        --pr                         Open a PR with `gh pr create --fill` (or reuse an existing one) first;
                                     skipped with a note if `gh` isn't installed
        --json                       Emit the documented JSON schema instead of plain text (see docs/README.finish.md)

Examples:
  workspace finish    # remove the worktree workspace you are in (session, worktree, config), once it is clean and pushed; the branch is kept
  workspace finish --pr    # open (or reuse) a PR for the branch first, then remove the workspace
  workspace finish --name myproject.worktree-PROJ-123    # finish a named worktree workspace, from anywhere
  workspace finish myproject.worktree-PROJ-123 --json    # the same, scripted; JSON on stdout
--- stderr
--- end

--- end

### workspace finish
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
